title: Unraveling in Guessing Games: An Experimental Study

source.title: Unraveling in Guessing Games: An Experimental Study

studies.title: Game · Guessing a fraction of the group average

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How deeply do people reason about others’ guesses, and how do they adjust after seeing what the group does?

fields.label: What the paper covers
fields.value: A repeated, incentivized number-guessing experiment with session-level multipliers, then analysis of first-round reasoning and learning.

fields.label: Across the paper
fields.value: Initial guesses were often far from equilibrium. After feedback, play moved in the predicted direction over later rounds, without implying that participants reached equilibrium.

fields.label: Expectation or comparison
fields.value: The bounded reasoning account predicts first-round guesses at a small number of iterations rather than at the fully iterated equilibrium.

fields.label: Interpretation and limits
fields.value: The groups play only four rounds. Interpreting clusters of guesses as a number of reasoning steps requires a model; the guesses do not directly reveal the thinking process.
fields.derivation: Scope of the published evidence and, where linked, differences from the Bench adaptation.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: Players choose a number from 0 to 100 simultaneously. The winner is closest to the group mean multiplied by the announced factor. Sessions use 1/2, 2/3 or 4/3. The same group plays four rounds and sees all anonymous guesses, the mean, the target and the winning number after each round.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: First-round responses are dispersed and often far from the equilibrium. The factor changes the direction in which the equilibrium logic pushes guesses.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: Compare the distribution of initial guesses with finite-depth reasoning predictions, then study adjustment after round feedback.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: Initial guesses cluster around a few steps of reasoning. Over rounds, guesses move in the direction of equilibrium; in the below-one games, medians generally fall.
